chunks: Zur‘ah narrated from Samā‘ah from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the Muslim: does he inherit from the polytheist? He said: “Yes. As for the polytheist, he does not inherit from the Muslim.”

key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِ: the Muslim, the legal subject discussed in the inheritance ruling
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكَ: the polytheist, the non-Muslim party in this ruling
key_terms.يَرِثُ: inherits; receives inheritance from an estate

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim inherit from a polytheist in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on inheritance between a Muslim and a polytheist. It states that a Muslim may inherit from a polytheist, while a polytheist does not inherit from a Muslim, making the rule one-directional in favor of the Muslim.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5722 - Zurah narrated from Samaah from Abu Abdullah (as) who said:

I asked Imam (as) whether a Muslim can inherit from a polytheist.
Imam (as) replied: "Yes, but a polytheist does not inherit from a Muslim."
